checks: Shared resources feed hosts, lampreys and non-host consumers; host support and harmful parasitism have different directions.
The response curve starts at s0 on the vertical axis, near 5/6, and decreases toward 1/2 within the stated s≥s0 domain.
Recruitment retains a host-dependent term; population feedback is not represented as individual sex change.
Only standardized resources and surviving-species count enter the ESI bracket.
notes: Conceptual scene, not a rerun of the paper’s empirical results.
Source inconsistencies remain in source_notes; no silent numeric reconstruction.
Publication-size typography and physical print proof remain author checks.

approval_evidence.scope: Selected figures 01–04 with requested local corrections and bilingual showcase only; not knowledge-base admission or independent scientific validation.

source_notes: Eq.12 is followed instead of Fig.7's conflicting resource-to-male sign.
The resource-share loop is a population/cohort mechanism, not individual sex change.
Biological shapes and response display are conceptual; no new simulation or field results.
